jd:
Full-stack engineer (Vue + Supabase)
Mid
Early product team building a digital ticketing product for Kenya intercity buses. Engineers own the passenger booking experience end to end: Postgres schema and Row Level Security on Supabase, plus a thin Vue client that talks to it. Hiring someone who can ship a credible MVP without a separate custom API layer unless they choose one.

Day to day:
- Model routes, trips, seats/capacity, and bookings in Postgres on Supabase
- Configure Auth and RLS so passengers only see and mutate their own bookings
- Build Vue screens for search, trip selection, and booking confirmation
- Seed enough Kenya corridor data to demo a real search → book path
- Leave clear run notes so a teammate can reproduce the demo locally or against a hosted project

Required skills:
- Comfortable building a Vue SPA that calls a backend over HTTP
- Can design a relational schema for trips and bookings and apply Supabase Auth + RLS
- Can prevent obvious double-booking (constraints, transactions, or explicit holds)
- Can document how to run the frontend and connect it to Supabase without leaking secrets

Nice to have:
- Supabase Edge Functions or RPC for atomic booking
- Seat-map UI beyond a simple remaining-capacity counter
- Local Supabase CLI workflow (supabase start / migrations)

Constraints:
- Assessment is a greenfield MVP — no starter app, schema, or seed data is provided on the desktop
- Primary UI must be Vue; primary backend must be Supabase (Postgres + Auth + RLS)
- Do not require a real payment gateway; booking may create a confirmed or held ticket record only
- Do not turn the challenge into operator fleet ops, live GPS tracking, or a multi-tenant marketplace
prompt: You are building Safari Coach, a small digital ticketing product for intercity buses in Kenya. There are no starter files on the desktop — design and implement everything yourself. Use Supabase for the backend (Postgres, Auth, RLS) and Vue for the frontend that points at it. Seed enough realistic Kenya routes/trips (prices in KES) that a reviewer can search the Nairobi–Mombasa corridor (example fare around 2500 KES) and at least one secondary corridor such as Nairobi–Kisumu, pick a trip, and complete a booking as a signed-in passenger. Payments are out of scope: a successful booking should persist a confirmed or held ticket without a real payment provider.
